newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end way above lows as shorts squeezed.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end way above lows as shorts squeezed.

text.p: Dutch shares closed slightly easier on Thursday after a volatile session which saw the AEX index open with a double figure loss only to creep into positive territory on a short squeeze before fading late in the day.

Dealers said the speed of Wednesday's 1.90 percent drop, and Thursday's early fall in response to Wall Street and dollar weakness had caught out some in the markets, sending options and cash market operators scrambling to cover short positions.
The AEX closed 1.38 points lower at 758.03, clawing back most of an early 10 point fall which sent the index below the 750 level for the first time in over a week.

"It looks like the market attracted a lot of bargain hunters after the opening fall," said one dealer. "People took the view that shares were going to be too cheap and stepped in because they couldn't afford to wait and see."

He added, however, that the market had seemed canted strongly towards the retail investor and that the short-term outlook appeared vulnerable, especially with Wall Street around 55 points lower by the time the Amsterdam market closed.
"It looks like there's a lot of hot money in the market at this point. It could still go down the same way that it did at the opening. It (volatility) is not all over yet," he said.

Another dealer said retail investors had shown buying interest immediately after the early fall, although institutions were taking a more cautious view because they were beginning to worry that Dutch interest rates may rise.
"Bargain hunting is a strong expression because the index is around 758. But compared to Tuesday (when the index closed at 774.20) people see these levels as a pretty good deal," he said.

Dealers said institutions were also looking to bank profits from a rally which had swept the AEX up more than 130 points since the beginning of the year. "The institutions are getting a bit cautious after so many gains," a dealer said.
